requirements.description: International split-unadjusted annual I/B/E/S detail forecast observations, forecast issue dates, analyst identifiers and fiscal-period identifiers. Apply the paper’s 12-month pre-fiscal-year-end window and retain the last annual forecast per analyst-firm-year; matched analyst-firm pairs are required for AFE/DISP/HORIZON while FOLLOW counts all analysts.

variable_coverage.construction: For each fiscal firm-year, match split-unadjusted annual I/B/E/S actual EPS to the median annual forecast from the matched analyst-firm set issued in the preceding 12 months, take the absolute error, and divide by the beginning-of-year stock price. Average over the pre- and post-adoption two-year windows and subtract pre from post; the paper scales ΔAFE by 100.

Construct DMAND from both annual standards histories, resolving source conflicts with annual-report checks, then multiply it by the High LAW–High IFRSdiff (LAW ≥ 1.6, IFRSdiff ≥ 11) country indicator using the cited 2005 LAW and Bae et al. country score. All three DMAND × group indicators are jointly included in every Eq. (2) outcome fit. The frozen equation cutoffs are preserved; Table 1 Panel B prose uses strict cutoffs for low groups.

Construct DMAND from both annual standards histories, resolving source conflicts with annual-report checks, then multiply it by the Low LAW–High IFRSdiff (LAW ≤ 1.6, IFRSdiff ≥ 11) country indicator using the cited 2005 LAW and Bae et al. country score. All three DMAND × group indicators are jointly included in every Eq. (2) outcome fit. The frozen equation cutoffs are preserved; Table 1 Panel B prose uses strict cutoffs for low groups.

Construct DMAND from both annual standards histories, resolving source conflicts with annual-report checks, then multiply it by the High LAW–Low IFRSdiff (LAW ≥ 1.6, IFRSdiff ≤ 11) country indicator using the cited 2005 LAW and Bae et al. country score. All three DMAND × group indicators are jointly included in every Eq. (2) outcome fit. The frozen equation cutoffs are preserved; Table 1 Panel B prose uses strict cutoffs for low groups.

At each firm-year beginning, derive market capitalization from the selected Global Compustat price/share data, convert to U.S. dollars with the I/B/E/S exchange rate effective at that beginning date, average within each two-year window, and take log(post average) minus log(pre average). The exact calendar-vs-fiscal year-start convention and issue/link choice remain unresolved.

Count all analysts with at least one annual forecast for each firm-year and form the log difference between average FOLLOW in the post and pre two-year windows; this is a control in AFE/DISP and the dependent variable in the ΔLogFOLLOW fit.

For each firm-year, average days from forecast issue date to the annual earnings announcement over forecasts; then take log average horizon in the post window minus log average horizon in the pre window. This control enters the AFE and DISP fits only.

evidence.quote: We obtain analysts’ forecast data from the IBES international (split unadjusted) database and accounting and market data from the Global Compustat or Datastream/Worldscope database.
evidence.description: Names the primary analyst forecast product and alternative accounting/market data families.

evidence.quote:
for a December year-end firm, the pre -mandatory-adoption window is 2003
and 2004, while the post -mandatory-adoption window is 2005 and 2006.
evidence.description: Provides the explicit December-year-end example; other fiscal-year endpoints are firm-specific.

evidence.quote:
For each firm-year, we retrieve all annual earnings forecasts
issued during the 12-month period prior to the year-end from each analyst covering the firm.
evidence.description: Defines annual forecast lookback and per-analyst firm-year selection base.

evidence.quote:
If an analyst issues more than one annual forecast for
a firm-year, we retain only the last forecast.
evidence.description: Defines forecast selection within analyst-firm-year.

evidence.quote: Thus, our sample is composed of a constant set of analyst-firm pairs matched across the pre - and post- mandatoryadoption windows.
evidence.description: Defines constant analyst-firm-pair composition for forecast outcomes.

evidence.quote:
We require that annual
earnings announcements be made no later than 240 calendar days after the
fiscal year-end.
evidence.description: Defines the announcement-date cutoff after fiscal year-end.

evidence.quote:
We exclude firms that were crosslisted in the United States as American Deposit Receipts (ADRs) during our
sample period based on the ADR databases of the Bank of New York and
Citibank.
evidence.description: Identifies the ADR exclusion source and event window.

evidence.quote:
We also exclude firms that changed their country of domicile or
primary exchange listing during our sample period.
evidence.description: Defines stable-domicile and primary-listing screens.

evidence.quote:
Next, to identify mandatory IFRS adopters, we obtain information on
firms’ accounting standards from both Global Compustat and Datastream/
Worldscope, and retain firms that reported under their domestic accounting standards during the two-year pre -mandatory-adoption window.
evidence.description: Both accounting-standard sources are required for mandatory-adopter identification.

evidence.quote:
When
Global Compustat and Datastream/Worldscope provide conflicting information as to which accounting standards a firm used, we verify data from
the firm’s annual reports.
evidence.description: The source requires annual-report review for conflicting standards fields.

evidence.quote: The control sample contains 250 firms.
evidence.description: Confirms the voluntary-adopter control population.

evidence.quote:
we select a control sample of European firms that voluntarily adopted IFRS
at least two years before the mandatory adoption deadline.
evidence.description: Defines the control firm adoption timing.

evidence.quote: by first calculating analysts’ absolute forecast error ( AFEit ) for each firmyear as: | Actual Earningsit - Median Forecastit |/ Stock Priceit,
evidence.description: Defines AFE numerator and price denominator.

evidence.quote: Stock Priceit is the stock price of firm i at the beginning of year t .
evidence.description: Anchors the price denominator at the beginning of year; calendar-vs-fiscal meaning is not stated.

evidence.quote: we first calculate forecast dispersion as: Standard Deviation of Forecasts/Stock
evidence.description: Defines forecast dispersion scaled by share price.

evidence.quote: We winsorize continuous variables at the 1% and 99% level
evidence.description: Defines winsorization thresholds.

evidence.quote: For each firm-year, we measure analyst following ( FOLLOW ) as the total number of analysts who issue at least one annual forecast for that firm-year.
evidence.description: Defines annual analyst-following count.

evidence.quote: Note that we include all analysts following a firm, not just the analysts included in our constant analyst-firm sample.
evidence.description: Distinguishes FOLLOW from the matched-analyst forecast outcomes.

evidence.quote:
a minimum of two analysts’ forecasts in each firm-year is needed to
measure dispersion
evidence.description: Defines the DISP sample screen.

evidence.quote: beginning-of-the-year market capitalization in U.S. dollars for each firm-year using the exchange rate in effect at the beginning of the year from I/B/E/S.
evidence.description: Defines beginning-of-year size and I/B/E/S exchange-rate input.

evidence.quote:
we first compute the average horizon (i.e., the number
of days between the forecast issuing date and the earnings announcement
date) across all forecasts for that firm-year.
evidence.description: Defines firm-year forecast horizon aggregation.

evidence.quote:
We use the “Rule of Law” ( LAW ) variable for 2005 from Kaufmann,
Kraay, and Mastuzzi [2007] as a proxy for the quality of countries’ legal
and enforcement regimes.
evidence.description: Defines cited 2005 country rule-of-law source.

evidence.quote:
We base our measure of the difference between a country’s accounting standards and IFRS on the gaapdiff1 measure of Bae, Tan, and
Welker[2008, table 1].
evidence.description: Defines the cited IFRS-difference source.

evidence.quote:
